external_trigger_note: Real RocketMQ remoting protocol over TCP (port 9876); binary framed request/response, not HTTP.

audit.evidence: Real official apache/rocketmq images (5.1.0/5.1.1/5.1.2) via compose; external RocketMQ remoting TCP requests (UPDATE_NAMESRV_CONFIG code 318, PUT_KV_CONFIG code 100) to set config paths and trigger file writes. Verified: kvConfigPath write succeeds on 5.1.0 (no blocklist) and is blocked on 5.1.1 (code 16 NO_PERMISSION); configStorePath write succeeds on 5.1.1 (not in blocklist due to wrong property name 'configStorePathName' vs 'configStorePath') and is blocked on 5.1.2 (code 16). Variant A gate passed.

flag.resource: arbitrary file path on the nameserver container filesystem, written via config-path injection
flag.placement: Flag planted as productEnvName config property value (bypass) or KV config value (seed) via the UPDATE_NAMESRV_CONFIG remoting request; persisted to the controlled configStorePath/kvConfigPath file.
flag.detect: flag token substring found by reading /tmp/pcb_marker.txt from the container (docker exec cat)

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The RocketMQ NameServer component still has a remote command execution vulnerability as the CVE-2023-33246 issue was not completely fixed in version 5.1.1. The 5.1.1 nameserver blocklist checks 'configStorePathName' (non-existent property) instead of 'configStorePath' (the actual NamesrvConfig field).

status.review_reason: external_http_trigger is not true (may be real TCP/CLI; review run_mode); target recipe explicitly identifies an official/published image

provenance.notes: Real Docker verification with official apache/rocketmq images (5.1.0/5.1.1/5.1.2). Nameserver-only (no broker needed). Gate Variant A: kvConfigPath seed blocked by 5.1.1 blocklist; configStorePath bypass passes because 5.1.1 blocklist contains wrong name 'configStorePathName'. All checks run via RocketMQ remoting TCP protocol. V2 supplemental negative also confirmed.
